label: prf:sl2-period-conserved-quantity
title: Proof of the depth-2 conserved first integral
html:
Write a_n := a_D^{(n)} and H_n = a_{n+1}^2 - \tau\,a_{n+1}a_n + a_n^2. For the single step, substitute the recurrence a_{n+2} = \tau a_{n+1} - a_n (Symplectic prolongation (det B = 1) gives a one-parameter recurrence) into H_{n+1}:

\begin{aligned}
H_{n+1}
&= a_{n+2}^2 - \tau\,a_{n+2}a_{n+1} + a_{n+1}^2 \\
&= (\tau a_{n+1} - a_n)^2 - \tau(\tau a_{n+1} - a_n)a_{n+1} + a_{n+1}^2 \\
&= \bigl(\tau^2 a_{n+1}^2 - 2\tau a_{n+1}a_n + a_n^2\bigr)
   - \bigl(\tau^2 a_{n+1}^2 - \tau a_{n+1}a_n\bigr) + a_{n+1}^2 \\
&= a_{n+1}^2 - \tau\,a_{n+1}a_n + a_n^2 \;=\; H_n .
\end{aligned}

This is the one-step invariance H_{n+1} = H_n: after substituting the recurrence, it is the polynomial identity above. A straightforward induction on n (base H_0 = H_0, step H_{k+1} = H_k = H_0) then gives H_n = H_0 for all n.

The first integral is exactly the quadratic form preserved by B \in \mathrm{Sp}(2) = \mathrm{SL}_2: in the basis (a_n, a_{n+1}) the map (a_n, a_{n+1}) \mapsto (a_{n+1}, \tau a_{n+1} - a_n) is B, and \det B = 1 is precisely the statement that B fixes the area form, of which H_n is the associated symmetric invariant.

Fork reading. Over \mathbb{R} with \tau = 2\cosh\theta > 2 the level set H_n = H_0 is a hyperbola; an orbit on it has a_{n+1}/a_n \to e^{\theta}, a constant — geometric growth, bounded ratio. The residue-sum period a_D^{(n)} = \sum_\lambda \dim_q (The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum) instead has a_{n+1}/a_n \to \infty (factorial growth from the square-root branch points of the colour cubic), so H_n \to \infty — it lies on no fixed conic and obeys no \det = 1 recurrence. Hence the depth-2 \tau is the n\le 4 effective germ, and the genuine prolongation kernel is the q-Bessel-class q-difference operator of The binding generating function's q-difference equation gives a depth-d recurrence. \qquad\blacksquare
